solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Gentry leg it shortly after meal with no starter? (10, two words)

indicators.note: having no starter means the opening letter of the meal word is dropped
shortly asks for the pronoun to appear in its clipped, apostrophised form as in old verse

parts.note: an evening meal
crus is the anatomical term for the lower leg, the shank
't is the shortened form of it, as in 'tis

explanation.surface: Some posh people are told to clear off quickly once dinner is over.
explanation.walkthrough: The supper loses its S; the leg is the anatomist's crus, and 'it shortly' is the poetic 't.
explanation.definitionFit: The upper crust is an idiom for the aristocracy or highest social class, which gentry also names.

clue.text: Crude rubber, originally lilac in colour

indicators.note: in places the selected letter inside the colour word

parts.note: a hue is a colour

indicators.note: originally points to the first letter of the following word

parts.note: the first letter of lilac

explanation.surface: A description of raw rubber whose colour starts out lilac.
explanation.definitionFit: Hule is a Spanish-derived name for the raw latex rubber from the Castilla tree.

clue.text: Female playwright's in character, one producing rewrite?

indicators.note: in places the playwright's name with its possessive inside the word for a role

parts.note: a part is a character in a play
Aphra Behn, the Restoration dramatist, plus the 's

explanation.surface: A woman dramatist is said to have assumed the role of someone revising a text.
explanation.walkthrough: Aphra Behn (1640-89) was one of the first English women to write professionally for the stage. APHRAS goes into PAR-T.
explanation.definitionFit: A paraphrast is a person who paraphrases, restating a text in different words.

clue.text: Perennial not active among variety of labiates

indicators.note: a variety of something is a different form of it, so the letters that follow are rearranged
not tells us the letter standing for active is absent from the word labiates

parts.note: A is the grammatical abbreviation for active (voice)

explanation.surface: A botanist notes some perennial that is dormant among a range of mint-family plants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not active' removes A from LABIATES, leaving LABITES; 'variety of' then rearranges those seven letters. Labiates are plants of the mint family, which makes the surface plausibly botanical.
explanation.definitionFit: An astilbe is a hardy herbaceous plant with feathery plumes that returns every year, so it is a perennial.

clue.text: Irritable

parts.note: surface reading: the plain dictionary meaning, short-tempered; setter's reading: this is the puzzle's competition entry, which solvers were invited to clue themselves, so no wordplay is printed

explanation.walkthrough: This was Azed's clue-writing competition word: the printed clue is only the definition, and solvers had to supply their own wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratty is British informal for bad-tempered or tetchy, a synonym of irritable.

clue.text: Source of syrup in a pastry dish (Italian) when one pleases (8, two words)

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in puts the syrup source inside the baked dish

parts.note: a pie is a pastry dish
acer is the maple genus, tapped for maple syrup

explanation.surface: A recipe note about where the syrup in an Italian tart comes from.
explanation.walkthrough: '(Italian)' tells you the answer is an Italian phrase; the acer is the maple tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A piacere is an Italian musical direction meaning at pleasure, letting the performer choose tempo freely.

clue.text: Strong drink? There's enough drunk when leaving university

indicators.note: drunk means unsteady and jumbled, so the letters of the word before it are reshuffled
the letter for university departs from the word enough before the reshuffle

explanation.surface: A drinker boasts that there is plenty of strong liquor downed once student days are over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when leaving university' takes U out of ENOUGH, giving ENOGH; 'drunk' rearranges those letters. Hogen is an archaic word found in Chambers.
explanation.definitionFit: Hogen (from hogen-mogen) is an old term for a potent Dutch-style liquor, so it names a strong alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: Mountaineer's aid? Half causing one to itch when climbing

indicators.note: in a down entry climbing means reading from bottom to top
half means only the first half of the word is kept

parts.note: prurient originally meant itching

explanation.surface: A climber's tool is said to make its user itch.
explanation.walkthrough: Prurient comes from Latin prurire, to itch. Its first half PRUR is read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A RURP (Realized Ultimate Reality Piton) is a tiny piton used in rock climbing.

clue.text: Excessively taking part in walk? I've had my share

indicators.note: taking part in means going inside the following word

parts.note: an allée is a tree-lined walk
OTT is over the top

explanation.surface: A rambler who has overdone it on a walk declares they have had enough.
explanation.walkthrough: An allée is a French-style avenue in a formal garden; the definition reads as the speaker's own words.
explanation.definitionFit: An allottee is a person who has been allotted, or given, a portion.

clue.text: Ageless jaunty? He'll surely have them (7, two words)

indicators.note: jaunty means sprightly and lively, so the letters skip into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cheery ageless person is surely well equipped.
explanation.walkthrough: Jaunty doubles as naval slang for the master-at-arms, which is why 'he' is sure to have the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea legs, the ability to stay steady on a rolling ship, are what any veteran sailor possesses.

clue.text: Change for Afghanis? Not quite a thrill

indicators.note: not quite means the word falls short by its last letter

parts.note: a pulse is a throb, a thrill

explanation.surface: Someone getting small change in Afghan currency finds it only a mild thrill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change' is small coins: the afghani is Afghanistan's currency and the pul its hundredth.
explanation.definitionFit: Puls are the small coins of Afghanistan, a hundred making one afghani.

clue.text: Lurker of old, person with inner swagger once

indicators.note: with inner means the second element sits inside the first

parts.note: per, as in so much per head, stands for each person
roul is an obsolete form of roll, to walk with a swagger

explanation.surface: A description of an old-time skulker with a self-important strut.
explanation.definitionFit: Prouler is an obsolete spelling of prowler, one who lurks or roams stealthily.

clue.text: Braidwork gal designed with tint alongside purl

indicators.note: designed means worked into a pattern, so the letters are arranged afresh

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
P is the knitting-pattern abbreviation for purl

explanation.surface: A woman creates braided work, dyed and knitted with purl stitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Platting is plaiting, the interweaving of strands into braids.

clue.text: Shilling and sovereign found circling street sewer

parts.note: s is the old abbreviation for a shilling

indicators.note: circling means going around, so the ruler word wraps the abbreviation

parts.note: an empress is a female sovereign
St is street

explanation.surface: Coins found lying around a road drain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sewer' reads as a drain but means one who sews. A shilling was a pre-1971 British coin worth twelve pence; a sovereign is also a gold coin, a further decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: A sempstress is an old spelling of seamstress, a woman who sews for a living.

clue.text: What makes Scot halfwit? It follows his recurrent stir

indicators.note: follows his places the word it after the reversed piece, which 'his' marks as the Scot's own stir
recurrent is read as running back again, so the Scots word is written backwards

parts.note: jee is a Scots word meaning to move or stir; 'his' points back to the Scot, so the stir is in his dialect

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about what turns a Scotsman into a fool, answered by his habit of stirring things up.
explanation.walkthrough: Jee is a Scots verb, to stir or budge, which is why 'his' ties the stir to the Scot; 'What makes' just introduces the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Eejit is the Scottish and Irish dialect form of idiot, a foolish person.

clue.text: Old pub sign, sheltered, bordering green, say?

indicators.note: bordering means lying on either side of what follows

parts.note: alee means on the sheltered side
a Green is a politician, a pol

explanation.surface: A historic inn sign, out of the wind beside the village green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green' looks like a village green but is a Green Party politician.
explanation.definitionFit: An ale-pole was a pole set up outside an alehouse to show that ale was sold there.

clue.text: Strangely well-behaved when maiden's involved

indicators.note: involved means wrapped inside, so the letter goes into the other word

parts.note: ruly, the opposite of unruly, means orderly
M stands for a maiden over in cricket

explanation.surface: Someone behaves oddly well when a young woman is around.
explanation.walkthrough: M goes inside RU-LY.
explanation.definitionFit: Rum means odd, so rumly is an adverb for doing something oddly.

clue.text: Doctor treated rib, poorly inside? What MMR should deal with

parts.note: MO is a medical officer

indicators.note: inside places the word for sick within the jumbled letters
treated means processed or worked on, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
poorly means unwell

explanation.surface: A medic tends a bad rib and asks what the triple vaccine covers.
explanation.walkthrough: MMR is the combined measles, mumps and rubella vaccine, which makes the definition fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Morbilli is the medical name for measles, the first disease the MMR vaccine targets.

clue.text: Leafy old ferns arranged at fringes of party

indicators.note: letters at the fringes of a word lie around its edges, wrapping it
arranged means put in a new order

parts.note: O is old, plus ferns
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Elderly ferns are positioned around the edges of a celebration as greenery.
explanation.walkthrough: Ferns in the surface tempt you towards the definition, but they are just letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Frondose means bearing fronds, so covered in leaf-like growth.

clue.text: Main line ma removed from family tree

indicators.note: removed from means taken out of the following word

parts.note: a stemma is a family tree or pedigree
taken as written

explanation.surface: A genealogist drops mother from the principal line of the family tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The stem is the main line of descent of a family, its principal branch.

clue.text: Wallops old snobs, left out of place

indicators.note: out of place says one letter of the word is shifted from its usual position

parts.note: snob is an old word for a shoemaker

explanation.surface: Someone hits some elderly social climbers, having been snubbed.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the L moves, from fifth place to second.
explanation.definitionFit: To clobber is to strike hard, so clobbers is a synonym for wallops.

clue.text: Unploughed strip one leaves neatly arranged bordering church

indicators.note: the rearranged letters border, i.e. surround on both sides, the abbreviation for church
arranged means put in a new order, so these letters are reshuffled
one leaves means that letter departs from the word that follows

parts.note: taken as written
A means one, as in a single item

explanation.surface: A tidily laid-out piece of untilled land lying next to a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One leaves' takes A out of NEATLY to leave NETLY; 'arranged' turns that into LYNET, which borders CH.
explanation.definitionFit: A lynchet is a terrace or bank of earth left on a hillside by ancient ploughing, a strip of land left unturned.

clue.text: Historical feudal system head of union disposed of

indicators.note: head of ... disposed of means the first letter is thrown out
disposed of means got rid of, so the named part goes

parts.note: marriage is a union

explanation.surface: An old feudal arrangement collapsed once the trade union leader was removed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union' looks like a trade union; here it is wedlock.
explanation.definitionFit: Arriage was a feudal service owed by tenants, chiefly work with horses or carts.

clue.text: Monster taking over central position in journalism, making headway

indicators.note: the monster takes over the middle spot of the word for journalism, replacing its central letter

parts.note: the press is a collective name for journalism and journalists
an ogre is a man-eating monster of folklore

explanation.surface: A monster muscles into the heart of the newspaper world and gets ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: The central letter of PRESS is E; OGRE replaces it.
explanation.definitionFit: Progress is forward movement or advance, the act of getting ahead or gaining ground.

clue.text: Cancel note replacing central section in exercise

indicators.note: the note's letters replace the middle letter of the word for exercise

parts.note: to exercise a power or right is to use it
NB, nota bene, is the abbreviation used to mark a note

explanation.surface: An instruction to strike out a note in the middle of a written exercise.
explanation.walkthrough: The note is NB, nota bene, not a musical letter; it replaces the middle S of USE.
explanation.definitionFit: Unbe is an archaic word meaning to cause to cease to exist, so to annul or cancel.

clue.text: Narrow rule kept within training school

indicators.note: kept within means held inside the next word

parts.note: a training camp
R is rule

explanation.surface: A strict regulation is enforced at a narrow-minded training school.
explanation.definitionFit: To cramp is to restrict or confine, as a verb matching narrow.

clue.text: Discontinued award, English, received by painter, is forgotten

indicators.note: received by means taken inside the following word
is forgotten tells you the letters of is are left out

parts.note: a painter is an artist
E is English

explanation.surface: A defunct English prize goes to a painter whose name nobody remembers.
explanation.walkthrough: IS leaves ARTIST to give AR-TT, with E inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Arett is an obsolete verb meaning to entrust or assign, hence an award no longer in use.

clue.text: Evil demon making adult alarmed locally

parts.note: A is adult, as in film certificates
frit is dialect for frightened

explanation.surface: A wicked spirit is scaring a grown-up in a regional story.
explanation.definitionFit: An afrit is a powerful malevolent spirit in Arabian mythology.

clue.text: Young offspring casting on dry fly?

indicators.note: casting means throwing off, so the next word is shed

parts.note: a scion is a young descendant
taken as written
arid means dry

explanation.surface: A child goes fly-fishing with a dry fly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Casting on' looks like knitting or angling; it means casting off ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A sciarid is a fungus gnat, a small fly of the family Sciaridae.

clue.text: Pupils once extracting nickel in chemical compound

indicators.note: extracting means pulling out, so the metal symbol is removed

parts.note: alumni are former pupils
Ni is the chemical symbol for nickel

explanation.surface: Former students remove a metal in a chemistry experiment.
explanation.definitionFit: Alum is a double sulphate salt of aluminium and potassium, used as an astringent.

clue.text: Note I have inscribed in French

indicators.note: inscribed in means written inside the next item

parts.note: Fr is French
I've

explanation.surface: Someone has written a message in French.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiver is a five-pound banknote, so a note in British slang.

clue.text: Tea not found when going round bun place bar that mentioned

indicators.note: not found says the tea letters are absent; this removes the final part of the word for tea
the tea letters go round what is left, so the front part of the word for tea comes off the start

parts.note: a Chelsea bun is named after the London district of Chelsea
cha is a slang word for tea; its first two letters come off here and its last letter in the next step
the final letter of cha, the word for tea

explanation.surface: A café-goer complains that tea is unavailable on a visit to a bakery, apart from what was said.
explanation.walkthrough: Tea is CHA, which is split around the answer in CHELSEA, a London district famous for a currant bun. 'when going round' strips CH from the front, leaving ELSEA; 'not found' then drops the final A.
explanation.definitionFit: Else means other than or besides, just as 'bar that mentioned' means excepting what has already been named.

clue.text: Gorgeous Labrador mostly trained with little energy

indicators.note: trained means disciplined into shape, so the letters are put into order
mostly means almost all, so the final letter is lost

parts.note: taken as written
E is energy

explanation.surface: A lovely Labrador, well trained but a bit lacking in pep.
explanation.definitionFit: Adorable means lovable and delightful, a near-synonym of gorgeous.

clue.text: Puts a fresh flame to Jock's chimney wreathed in endless smoke (his?)

indicators.note: wreathed in means surrounded by, so the chimney goes inside
endless means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: reest is Scots for to dry in smoke
lum is Scots for chimney

explanation.surface: A Scotsman relights his fire, his chimney enveloped in smoke.
explanation.walkthrough: '(his?)' says the smoke word is also Scots. Jock is a nickname for a Scotsman.
explanation.definitionFit: To relume is to rekindle or relight, which is giving a fresh flame.

clue.text: China trinkets prompting little chat

definitions.meaning: first meaning: heraldic souvenir china made by W.H. ...
second meaning: slang clipping of a word for idle talk

explanation.surface: Ornaments on a mantelpiece give rise to some small talk.
explanation.walkthrough: Goss china was crested souvenir ware from Stoke; the slang is short for gossip.
explanation.definitionFit: Goss names collectable crested porcelain ornaments and is also informal for tittle-tattle.

clue.text: It assesses pace of green — possibly tempts rim round its centre

indicators.note: possibly means in one possible arrangement, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the centre of the earlier word means its middle letter

parts.note: the middle letter of green, which 'its' refers to

explanation.surface: A device measuring how quick a golf green runs might lure the ball round the hole's edge.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram letters wrap the middle of green; 'its' points back to green.
explanation.definitionFit: A Stimpmeter is a ramp used in golf to measure the speed at which a putting surface runs.
